title: Merge duplicate failure classes instead of only adding new ones
summary: Sri's note (BRIEF.md, 2026-11-08) says the introspection step only ever adds failure classes (158 so far, none merged). I read it as: make the class registry merge-capable and stop code adding near-duplicates. The audience is Sri and the introspection and planner prompts that read the class list.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require passing cargo test, clippy and fmt.
The fix is at class creation, which is where the duplicates come from, plus a merge path.
Criteria run tests that show reuse and merge happening.
Dedupe is enforced in code rather than by prompt.
Docs and the decision entry are written for an outside reader.
Scoped to one mechanism and leaves the data migration out.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs (entry: the introspection answer handler around lines 1570-1620 where `failure_class == "new"` mints a FailureClass with ClassStatus::Proposed and a fresh RecordId; the registry is read at lines 424-434 from records/failure-classes; Jev class matching runs in shadow via ask_jev, then code narrows by class_of_work and category), crates/athena-data/src/records/introspection.rs (ClassStatus has only `Proposed`; FailureClass is deny_unknown_fields), crates/athena-core/src/labeled.rs and hestia.rs (they read classes, so merged classes must resolve to their target when counting recurrence). The records validation allow-list already accepts athena.failure-class/1 through AnyRecord; any new field or status variant must round-trip in the existing records round-trip test and check_record_file. Class count and recurrence are measured directly on a fixture registry in tests, not through a stand-in.
Existing code: docs/design/defaults-loop.md section 3.4 already says the user may rename or merge classes, but no code does; this job builds that merge and extends the introspect.rs registry path.

The real 158 classes live under records/, which this job cannot read or edit. So the job delivers the mechanism (a merge status, resolution of merged ids, duplicate prevention at creation) and does not rewrite existing records.
Term ladder: not used. Merge means a class record marked merged into a target class id; counts and lookups then treat it as its target.

Assumed mechanism: add `ClassStatus::Merged` with an optional `merged_into` id, a code path that refuses to create a new class whose normalised name equals an existing live class (reusing it instead), and resolution of merged ids in registry reads, earlier-case selection and recurrence counts. A CLI command for a user-driven merge is optional and only added if small.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) need no change.

acceptance_criteria.text: `cargo test -p athena-core introspect` includes a test where a new-class answer whose normalised name equals an existing live class reuses that class id and adds no registry record.
A test merges class B into class A. Registry reads and earlier-case selection then count B's introspections under A, and the live class count drops by one. Run with `cargo test -p athena-core`.

A FailureClass with status merged and merged_into round-trips through the records round-trip test and passes check_record_file. An old `proposed` record still deserializes. Run with `cargo test -p athena-data`.
`cargo test` passes workspace-wide, `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
docs/design/defaults-loop.md section 3.4 and CHANGELOG.md describe the merge behavior. They say the existing 158 classes are not rewritten by this change and mark any unbuilt part as design.
A decision entry in docs/decisions.md records the call: dedupe at creation plus merge status, with the alternatives of periodic model clustering and a manual-only merge, and why.

out_of_scope: Rewriting or merging the existing 158 records under records/
Clustering existing classes with a model
Changing the lessons-into-defaults or skills work in the other brief lines
Prompt file edits (token headroom is near zero)
departures: The request is a statement rather than an instruction, so there is a higher chance the user wanted a different fix. The change also touches the record schema across several crates, which is costlier than the reference.
hard_reason: It changes how the introspection pipeline assigns failure classes and the record schema that feeds the defaults loop, scoring and the scope guard, so a mistake is hard to see.
